messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert -> oncall jamie. High 401 spike originating from idp auth checks (prod). Please investigate ASAP.

jamie: on it, joining bridge. what metrics do we have?

incident-bot: spike started ~5m ago. ~20x baseline 401s to /v1/auth/validate, same issuer header, mixed UA strings. Sample UA: 'curl/7.68.0', 'kube-probe/1.20'.

sara: seeing matching telemetry — spikes correlate with debug log shipper events from staging-forwarder.

jamie: pulling edge-proxy logs now. alex can you grep last 10m for 401+issuer and user_agent counts?

alex: quick run shows repeated Authorization header fragments in recent staging debug files. snippet: `s3://staging-logs/2026-03-18/debug-01.log` includes lines with Authorization: Bearer <redacted-token-frag>.

sara: that suggests a log-forwarder misconfig shipped sensitive headers to staging. likely exfil. we should assume tokens leaked until proven otherwise.

jamie: mitigation plan: 1) add WAF UA block for suspicious UAs, 2) rate-limit auth-validate endpoint, 3) rotate service tokens for edge-proxy and staging-forwarder, 4) isolate and suspend staging-forwarder, 5) start KMS rotation for issuer keys. agree?

lia: communications — open a P1 incident bridge? I'll prep customer comms drafts but need legal signoff.

legal: preserve evidence, no external disclosure until we confirm scope. redact specifics in public comms.

devops-runner: queued token rotate for svc-proxy: `kubectl set secret svc-proxy-token v2 --from-literal=token=REPLACE_ME` -> rolling restart will take ~90s per pod.

jamie: applying UA block now: edge-proxy rule blocking regex (curl|kube-probe|python-requests). applying rate-limit 50r/s on auth-validate for anonymous clients.

sara: starting forensic snapshot of implicated buckets. commands: `aws s3 cp s3://staging-logs/... /forensics/staging-logs/` and `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=staging-forwarder`.

alex: found two external sink endpoints in forwarder config: logs-external.example.com and 3.35.120.11; isolating service account and revoking its IAM keys now.

jamie: revocation in progress. will also rotate any tokens created by that svcacct. lia, legal, flag customers who may be affected based on customer IDs in those logs.

lia: drafting template for potential affected customers. will not send until legal confirms wording.

incident-bot: added reminder -> handoff to next oncall @morgan in ~2h.

jamie: summary update: blocking suspicious traffic, rotated svc-proxy tokens, suspended staging-forwarder, revoking IAM keys, starting KMS issuer key rotation, evidence copied to forensic bucket. impact: transient 401s for some customers during roll, potential token exposure under investigation.

sara: forensics lead accepted. capturing memory for forwarder pod, exporting logs, preserving exact object versions.

alex: confirm all staging-forwarder pods terminated and deleted. pointing any retries to dead-letter rather than external sink.

morgan: taking over for next shift. jamie, paste runbook/checklist and status.

jamie: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/auth-leak-response (internal). Completed steps: 1) UA block 2) rate-limit 3) svc token rotate started/completed for proxy 4) staging-forwarder suspended 5) IAM keys revoked 6) KMS rotation initiated 7) evidence copied. Open tasks: complete KMS rotation, verify no additional sinks, final customer impact assessment, legal review for disclosure.

morgan: ack. I'll validate KMS rotation progress and coordinate customer-impact scoring. keep channel posted.

lia: will keep comms draft in /incidents/1736543210/comm-drafts and ping legal for approval.

legal: reviewing. please freeze related S3 objects and do not delete until we finish chain-of-custody steps.

jamie: leaving bridge but reachable. marking incident status -> containment. will reconnect on handoff. :white_check_mark:
